sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE VISHAL MISHRA  ON THE 9 th OF MAY, 2025
CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 3683 of 2025  NARAYAN SHRIVAS

Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Ghanshyam Pandey - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Sumit Raghuwanshi - Govt. Advocate for respondent N

ORDER This criminal appeal is filed under Section 14A(1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 against the order dated 29.03.2025 passed by the Special Judge,
Jabalpur (M.P.) whereby the appellant's application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail relating to Crime No.120 of 2025 registered at Police Station Bargi District Jabalpur for the offence under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(f), 3(1)(g) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act, has been rejected.
2. The allegations against the present appellant, in short, are that he is the signatory of the sale deed of the land belonging to Scheduled Tribes community which has been executed in favour of the co-accused and accordingly defrauded the actual landowner by preparing forged and fabricated documents in connivance with the co-accused.
3.

sentences.text:
It is argued that the appellant aged about 78 years and suffering from NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:22529 2 CRA-3683-2025 various ailments, has not committed any offence.
He has been falsely implicated due to prevailing animosity.
He is in custody since 27.03.2025.
As the charge sheet has been filed, there is no further requirement of custodial interrogation.
He has been implicated on the basis of memorandum of other co-accused.
The main allegation is against co-accused Ganga Pathak who asked the appellant to become a witness in the sale deed.

sentences.text: appellant is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering the bail application.
4. Counsel appearing for the appellant has further submitted that wife of the appellant is seriously ill and recently she has undergone surgical operation.
For this, various medical documents have been placed on record.

It is submitted that as there is no other family member to look after her, the appellant may be released on bail.
5.

Per contra, State counsel has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail pointing out the fact that the appellant has actively participated in the commission of the offence and has received an amount of Rs. 10,000/- for becoming a signatory to the sale deed.
The case in hand pertains to illegal sale of land belonging to the members of SC/ST community.

By playing fraud and preparing forged and fabricated documents in connivance with the other co-accused, the sale deeds have been executed with the help of the appellant and without the consent of members of SC/ST community.

It is submitted that the appellant has previous criminal antecedent being Crime No. 93 of 2025 registered at Police Station Tilwara District Jabalpur for the offence under Sections 419, 420, 467,
468, & 471 of IPC and Sections 3(1) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:22529 3 CRA-3683-2025 (f), 3(1)(g) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act
, so he is not entitled for bail.

6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and the role played by the appellant in the commission of the offence, but without commenting upon the merits of the case, this Court does not deem it appropriate to enlarge the appellant on bail, even on medical grounds.
7. Accordingly, the appeal stands dismissed.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE VV Narayan Shrivas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94682478/
